prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_D:
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2001 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core principles: Freedom, Justice, Honesty. Government should enable people by delivering high‑quality public services, devolving power, and embedding a “green thread” across all policy.

Health:
- Cut waiting times by recruiting 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied professionals, plus 10,000 beds; £1,000 annual pay boost for lowest‑paid NHS staff.
- Prioritise prevention: free dental and eye checks, more scanning equipment, £500m for NHS dentistry, wider in‑practice testing, support complementary medicine.
- End charges for long‑term personal care; create a Pharmaceutical Agency to end the postcode lottery and lower drug costs; aim to reduce/abolish prescription charges.
- Patient Care Guarantees; stronger local accountability; independent advocates; no‑fault compensation; ban age discrimination; end mixed wards.

Education, skills and jobs:
- Primary classes to average 25; 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants (focus on Key Stage 1); paid preparation time; teacher training salary; scrap SATs at 7; reduce bureaucracy.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for poorest; raise loan repayment threshold; improve academic pay equality.
- Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 2 for adults; Level 3 for 16–24s); simpler FE funding/qualifications.
- Replace New Deal with a flexible, combined Benefits and Jobs Agency; study leave with pay for 16–24s; SME training incentives.

Law and order:
- 6,000 extra police; 2,000 part‑time retained community officers; Community Safety Force for nuisance crime; independent police complaints system.
- Focus prisons on work, skills and rehabilitation; expand effective community sentences; cut reoffending.
- Strengthen victims’ rights; keep jury trial; end most mandatory sentences; tackle hate crime.

Transport:
- Free off‑peak bus travel for pensioners/disabled; aim half‑price for under‑19s in education.
- Abolish VED for the cleanest vehicles; no real‑terms fuel duty rise next Parliament; empower congestion charging/parking levies to fund public transport.
- Sustainable Transport Authority; stronger regulation; restructure Railtrack into a public‑interest model; modernise Underground via not‑for‑profit bonds; rural transport fund.
- Double rail freight by 2010; curb road building in sensitive areas; promote cleaner vehicles.

Pensions, wages and benefits:
- Raise basic pension (+£5; more for over‑75/80); create Independent Pensions Authority; relax annuity rules; reduce means‑testing.
- Review minimum wage annually and apply full rate from age 16.
- Extra support for children on long‑term income support; replace CSA with family courts; extend Winter Fuel Payment to severely disabled; long‑term goal to zero the 10p tax band for low earners.

Business, consumers and green economy:
- Cut red tape; small business rates allowance; tougher competition law (esp. local monopolies, banking); stronger consumer protection.
- Shift taxes from “goods” to pollution: move toward a carbon tax; 10% UK renewables by 2010 (rising annually); phase out nuclear at end of life; expand energy efficiency.

Constitution and civil liberties:
- Fair votes: AV+ referendum for Westminster (ultimately STV); STV for local/European elections; elected Senate; stronger Parliament and FOI; votes at 16.
- Equality Act and Commission; repeal Section 28; stronger privacy/surveillance safeguards; humane, faster asylum system, end vouchers; more devolution and local income tax.

Communities, rural/urban:
- One‑stop regeneration grants; protect local services; brownfield‑first with VAT/business rate reform; national recycling programme; CAP/CFP reform; create a Ministry for Rural Affairs.

Europe, foreign policy and defence:
- Pro‑EU reform: constitution to define powers, greater transparency, enlargement, stronger CFSP; euro entry via referendum at a sustainable rate.
- End subsidies for arms exports; 0.7% aid target; faster debt relief; fair trade with environmental safeguards; support ICC/UN peacekeeping.
- Maintain defence spending; flexible, deployable forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; oppose US NMD.

TEXT_F:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2001: “Time for Common Sense” — Summary

Core vision
- Trust people over government: devolve power, cut taxes and regulation, and free public services from political micromanagement.
- Strengthen families, local institutions, charities, and national identity; be “in Europe, not run by Europe.”

Families and education
- Tax cuts focused on early years: raise Children’s Tax Credit by £200; new Married Couple’s Allowance (transferable personal allowance) worth up to £1,000 for families with children under 11 or carers; remove tax on widowed parents’ allowances; reform Working Families Tax Credit to pay the caring parent.
- Create “Free Schools”: full autonomy for heads/governors; less bureaucracy; easier exclusions with Progress Centres for disruptive pupils; more per‑pupil funding direct to schools; allow successful schools to expand and new faith/parent/charity/company schools to open; parents can trigger Ofsted and management change.
- Universities: endowment funds for independence; no top‑up fees; student loan repayments only above £20,000 income.

Crime and justice
- More police; cut red tape; visible policing (“cops in shops”) and parish constables; target antisocial behaviour.
- Persistent young offenders: 10x more Secure Training Centre places; link release to qualifications/behaviour.
- Tougher drug laws: mandatory jail for dealing to under‑16s; harsher near schools.
- Honest sentencing (end automatic and special early release); prisoners to work; lifetime supervision possible for sex offenders; protect children online.
- Strengthen victims’ rights and clarify self‑defence/double jeopardy.

Economy and tax
- £8bn annual tax cuts funded by savings outside schools/NHS/police/defence: abolish tax on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; cut petrol/diesel duty by 6p; restore Married Couple’s Allowance; business reliefs; abolish IR35.
- Simpler, more transparent public accounts; National Accounts Commission; clearer tax statements.
- Deregulation: independent Deregulation Commission with departmental regulatory budgets; exemptions for small firms; scrap Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear.
- Keep the pound; strengthen BoE MPC independence; Council of Economic Advisers; spending growth within trend GDP.

Health
- Match NHS spending plans but end micromanagement; Patient’s Guarantee: clinically set maximum waits (starting with cancer/cardiac), with choice of NHS or private treatment if breached.
- Restore ward sister/matron authority; GP and patient choice of hospital; encourage GP specialisation; allow proven complementary therapies; increase hospice funding; expand high-throughput surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund for costly drugs.

Older people and care
- Cut tax on savings; raise age allowance; increase basic pension (extra for over‑75s); optional consolidation of winter fuel/TV licence into higher, tax‑free pension.
- Abolish compulsory annuity purchase at 75; explore funded pension option for young workers; protect assets of those who pre‑fund long‑term care.

Europe, defence, and asylum
- Keep veto; reject euro; renegotiate Nice; embed “reserved powers” in UK law; complete single market; tackle EU fraud.
- Back NATO; oppose EU army outside NATO; meet full manning; exempt forces from ECHR; support missile defence; maintain independent deterrent.
- Asylum: secure reception centres until decisions; presume refusal from safe countries; dedicated Removals Agency.

Welfare and civil society
- Office of Civil Society; abolish charities’ irrecoverable VAT (funded by euro‑prep budgets).
- Replace New Deal with “Britain Works,” paying providers for jobs gained and sustained; “Can Work, Must Work.”
- Expect lone parents with children 11+ to seek suitable work; better savings rules and return‑to‑work support for disabled; national anti‑fraud squad; clean up NI numbers.

Town, country, transport, environment
- Foot and Mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP; clearer food origin labelling; cut rural business rates; support post offices via benefit card; abolish top‑down housebuilding targets; “Blue Belts” for waterways; urban Regeneration Companies; expand homeownership.
- Transport: 6p fuel duty cut; long-term investment; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe; charge foreign lorries (Brit Disc); revive rail; support London Underground reform.

Culture, media, sport
- £3bn endowment for arts/heritage (Channel 4 privatisation + Lottery surpluses); boost tourism; protect school sport and playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs; single communications regulator; liberalise ownership; fair BBC regulation.

Constitution and governance
- Devolve power to best councils (“free councils”); local referendums for big tax rises; scrap regional agencies/assemblies; English Votes for English Laws; strengthen Lords via independent appointments and elected element; tougher Commons scrutiny; keep FPTP; reduce ministers/MPs/spads; uphold Belfast Agreement with decommissioning.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_F aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.
